It builds on the project's existing WHATWG tokenizer (`walkHtmlTokens`) and adds the tree-construction layer. ## Summary `buildHtmlAst(html)` returns a `DocumentNode` (`{ type: "document", children }`) and exposes `NS_HTML = 0`, `NS_MATHML = 1`, `NS_SVG = 2` as properties. **How it works** — it drives `walkHtmlTokens` with callbacks and maintains a stack of open elements: - **Elements** get `type`, `tagName` (lowercased), `children`, `attributes`, `selfClosing`, `namespace`, and `end`. Attributes are accumulated from `attribute` callbacks (they fire before `openTag`) and decoded via the tokenizer's `decodeHtmlEntities` (empty string when valueless; unquoted values handled by returning the right positions). - **Void elements** (`img`, `br`, `input`, …) are `selfClosing: true` with no children and aren't pushed. In foreign (SVG/MathML) content, a trailing `/` also self-closes; in HTML it's ignored for non-void tags per spec. - **Text** merges adjacent segments at the same level and is entity-decoded — except inside raw-text elements (`script`, `style`, etc.), where content is preserved verbatim as a single `TextNode`. - **Comments** strip `` (or `--!>`); bogus comments (e.g. `` auto-closes on a block-level start tag; `
